title: Putin seeks a Ukraine summit with Trump and Xi
deck: Moscow wants a three-way summit in China on a Ukraine deal while refusing to meet Zelensky, and Kyiv and Europe fear being bargained over rather than bargained with.

fuel.title: Patriot sign-off stalls while Oleshky truce holds
fuel.how: Zelensky says Hegseth took a month to approve Patriot missiles, which shows how much Kyiv's air defence depends on Washington, even as a US-brokered local ceasefire gives talks a template.

fuel.title: Trilateral talks to restart, summit prepared
fuel.how: Zelensky says talks with Russia and the US will restart and Ukraine wants Abu Dhabi moved earlier with the EU at the table, while Moscow pushes a different format of Putin, Trump and Xi.

fuel.title: Trump and Zelensky split over oil strikes
fuel.how: The two leaders disagree over Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil, which exposes a split over how much pressure to put on Moscow before any deal.

fuel.title: Russian deficit doubles as Gulf war competes
fuel.how: A 2026 deficit near twice the plan raises Moscow's incentive to deal, while the war with Iran splits Washington's attention and money.

card.headline: Putin wants to settle Ukraine with Trump and Xi, without Zelensky in the room

keyNumber.label: how long Zelensky says Hegseth took to sign off on Patriot missiles for Ukraine

forYou.line: Interceptor supply is the bottleneck; US approvals, not Ukrainian demand, set the pace.
Oil-strike disputes and the Gulf war keep supply risk priced in; a real ceasefire could ease Black Sea risk, but not soon.
A US-China-Russia deal struck without allies is a tail risk for European defence and Ukraine-funding plans.
A local ceasefire in Oleshky began on 27 October. Whether it widens is the first real test of Moscow's intent.

effects.text: Kremlin says preparations are under way for a Putin-Xi-Trump summit in China; Putin still refuses to meet Zelensky
Zelensky says trilateral talks with Russia and the US will restart; Kyiv pushes to pull the Abu Dhabi round forward and bring in the EU
US-brokered ceasefire takes effect in Oleshky for evacuations and aid; Moscow floats copying the model elsewhere
Trump and Zelensky clash over Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil
Washington's choices on Patriots, intelligence sharing and Starlink become bargaining chips, whatever the intent

whatHappened: On 19 October, Putin proposed a summit with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping on a Ukraine deal while again refusing to meet Volodymyr Zelensky. The same day, Secretary of State Marco Rubio denied there had been any pause in US intelligence sharing with Ukraine.

By 25 October, headlines said the Kremlin was preparing a Putin-Xi-Trump summit in China and that Moscow, Beijing and Washington were ready in principle. The obvious venue is the APEC leaders' meeting in Shenzhen on 18-19 November, which Trump plans to attend. We have not seen a confirmed date for a three-way meeting.

On 26 October, Zelensky called out a monthlong wait for Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to sign off on Patriot missiles, and Trump and Zelensky were reported to clash over Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil. Zelensky also said trilateral talks with Russia and the US would restart.

On 27 October, a US-brokered local ceasefire began in the occupied town of Oleshky, in the Kherson region, to allow evacuations and aid. Reports credit First Lady Melania Trump with securing it. Russia says it does not intend to halt hostilities elsewhere while talks go on.
whyItMatters: Security: Ukraine's air defence depends on decisions in Washington. A month's wait on Patriot approval shows the leverage the US holds, at a time when Russian long-range attacks are intensifying; the UN reported at least 14 civilians killed overnight into 22 October. The Oleshky truce is the first concrete sign of a model that could widen, but it is local and humanitarian.

Politics: Putin wants a format with the two biggest powers and without Kyiv or Europe. Zelensky is pushing the opposite, with Europe at the table, and has publicly rejected neutrality and limits on his army. The talks matter in Europe too: Ukraine aid is now a central issue in France's 2027 campaign, and Italy's Meloni says support for Ukraine is what makes peace possible.

Energy: Trump and Zelensky disagree over strikes on Russian oil, so the two governments are not aligned on how hard to press Moscow. Oil is also where the second war bites: Gulf fighting since February has kept fuel and freight prices high, and French diesel hit a record EUR 2.41 a litre in September.

Public money: Russia's government projects a 2026 deficit of 7.3 trillion rubles, nearly double the plan, with defence set to take more than a third of 2027 spending. That is pressure on Moscow to deal. In the West, money and attention are split between Ukraine and Iran, and a Democratic House after 3 November could shape what the US can offer.

winners.why: A summit with Trump and Xi lifts Russia's status, sidelines Kyiv and Europe, and costs nothing if Moscow keeps fighting during talks.
As APEC host, China controls the stage and could be the broker or arbiter in a great-power deal.
The local ceasefire allows evacuations and aid deliveries in a town described as on the brink of disaster.
Demand for interceptors stays far ahead of supply.

losers.why: Zelensky is excluded from Putin's proposed format and depends on US decisions for interceptors, intelligence and communications.
They fear a deal over their heads on sanctions, borders and security guarantees, while funding most of the aid.
Long-range attacks are intensifying and Russia says it will not pause fighting during talks.

losers.who: Households in Europe and the US
losers.why: Fuel and food prices stay high while two wars compete for attention and money.

whatsNext: 29 October: first reading of Russia's budget in the Duma.
1 November: Bulgaria's presidential run-off, where the Ukraine war divides voters.
3 November: US midterms; a Democratic House would hold the purse strings on Ukraine aid from January.
Early November, date unconfirmed: trilateral talks with Russia and the US are due to restart; Kyiv wants Abu Dhabi moved forward.
18-19 November: APEC in Shenzhen, the likeliest venue if a Putin-Xi-Trump meeting happens.

predict.question: Before you read the scenarios: what is the most likely outcome by the end of 2026?
options: Talks continue and local truces spread, but fighting goes on
A Putin-Xi-Trump summit produces a signed framework deal
Talks collapse and the US cuts support
predict.explanation: Our base case, at about 45%, is talks without a general ceasefire: Russia says it will not halt hostilities while negotiating, the BBC's Russia editor judges Putin is under no pressure to end the war, and the Oleshky model may spread only in small steps.

timeline.title: US strikes on Iran begin
timeline.detail: The Gulf war starts to compete with Ukraine for US attention, weapons and money, and keeps oil and freight costs high for months.

timeline.title: Xi's state visit to Washington ends
timeline.detail: A 'constructive relationship of strategic stability' is declared, with few concrete trade deliverables. It sets up the Trump-Xi channel Moscow now wants to use.

timeline.title: Russia submits a three-year budget
timeline.detail: The 2026 deficit is projected at 7.345 trillion rubles, nearly double the plan; the first Duma reading is set for 29 October.

timeline.title: Trump says he may meet Kim Jong Un on his Asia trip
timeline.detail: Kim's missile tests continue; North Korea's troops-for-technology alliance with Moscow links the two bids for a Trump meeting.

timeline.title: Putin proposes a summit with Trump and Xi, refuses to meet Zelensky
timeline.detail: Rubio denies there was any pause in US intelligence sharing with Ukraine.

timeline.title: Russia agrees to talks but sees little to discuss
timeline.detail: The BBC's Russia editor writes that Putin does not feel under pressure to end the war.

timeline.title: Russian long-range attacks intensify
timeline.detail: UN News reports at least 14 civilians killed and 78 injured overnight, including in Kyiv.

timeline.title: Zelensky says Starlink limits still affect Ukrainian forces
timeline.detail: US officials and Elon Musk give conflicting accounts of who controls access. Ukraine later said the connection was restored on 24 October.

timeline.title: Kremlin says preparations begin for a Putin-Xi-Trump summit in China
timeline.detail: Headlines say Moscow, Beijing and Washington are 'ready in principle'. Allied commentators call it a possible new Yalta. No date is confirmed.

timeline.title: Zelensky calls out a monthlong Patriot approval wait
timeline.detail: Kyiv presses for more interceptors against missiles and jet-powered drones. Trump and Zelensky also clash over oil strikes.

timeline.title: Oleshky ceasefire takes effect
timeline.detail: Russia halts strikes on the town for evacuations and aid; reports credit Melania Trump with brokering it. Putin's office floats expanding the model.

causes.name: Great-power bargaining
causes.detail: Putin wants a settlement made by the strongest states rather than by Kyiv and Europe.

causes.name: Dependence on US systems
causes.detail: Ukraine relies on Washington for Patriot interceptors, intelligence and communications links, so US decisions double as leverage.

causes.name: Russia's war economy
causes.detail: Defence is set to take more than a third of federal spending in 2027 at a record 17.1 trillion rubles, with oil revenue falling.

causes.name: Putin's summit proposal
causes.detail: Announced on 19 October alongside a refusal to meet Zelensky.

causes.name: Trump-Xi calendar
causes.detail: Xi's Washington visit in September and the Shenzhen APEC meeting on 18-19 November give a ready venue.

causes.name: US-Ukraine friction
causes.detail: A monthlong Patriot approval wait, a clash over oil strikes, and Starlink restrictions with Musk alleging a terms breach, which Kyiv denies.

causes.name: Escalating Russian strikes
causes.detail: Intensified long-range attacks raise the human cost of every week without a ceasefire.

causes.name: US midterms and Gulf war
causes.detail: Domestic politics and the Iran conflict split attention and funding.

causes.name: Local-truce template
causes.detail: The Oleshky ceasefire shows a US-brokered pause is possible and may be a model for wider talks.

stakeholders.name: Vladimir Putin
stakeholders.wants: A settlement brokered by Trump and Xi that locks in gains, and 1997-style limits on NATO, as one report claims
stakeholders.leverage: Ongoing offensives; no sign he feels pressure to stop; the ability to offer local pauses
stakeholders.likelyMove: Accept talks and local truces, refuse a general halt, keep Zelensky out of the room

stakeholders.name: Donald Trump
stakeholders.wants: A deal he can call his own, without losing attention on Iran or votes at home
stakeholders.leverage: Patriots, intelligence sharing, Starlink-linked access and sanctions
stakeholders.likelyMove: Keep both channels open, push Kyiv on terms, and meet Xi in Shenzhen on 18-19 November

stakeholders.name: Xi Jinping
stakeholders.wants: Tariff relief and a bigger say in the post-war order
stakeholders.leverage: Host's control of the Shenzhen agenda; economic ties to Russia
stakeholders.likelyMove: Welcome a three-way meeting in principle while avoiding blame for its outcome

stakeholders.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
stakeholders.wants: Talks with Europe at the table, security guarantees, and no neutrality or army caps
stakeholders.leverage: Domestic resolve, European backing, and Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil
stakeholders.likelyMove: Push to bring Abu Dhabi talks forward, keep the US on side, and criticise delays publicly

stakeholders.name: European leaders (Macron, Meloni, EU institutions)
stakeholders.wants: A seat at the table and no deal over their heads
stakeholders.leverage: EU funding channels, sanctions and the Coalition of the Willing
stakeholders.likelyMove: Press for inclusion, as Meloni told the Senate that support is what makes peace possible

stakeholders.name: Marine Le Pen and the French far right
stakeholders.wants: End Ukraine funding within six months and cap France's EU contribution at EUR 5bn
stakeholders.likelyMove: Treat a Putin-Trump-Xi deal as proof that Europe should step back

stakeholders.name: US Democrats in Congress
stakeholders.wants: Oversight of Ukraine aid and limits on a bargain over allies
stakeholders.leverage: The power of the purse if they win the House on 3 November
stakeholders.likelyMove: Contest any summit deal that trades away Ukraine aid

sectors.why: Kyiv is pressing for more interceptors against missiles and jet-powered drones, and approvals are the bottleneck.
Strikes on Russian oil and the Gulf war keep supply risk priced in; a real ceasefire or a deal on those strikes would change it.
A 2026 deficit of 7.3 trillion rubles and defence above a third of 2027 spending leave little room.
Ukraine funding runs largely through EU channels, so the next seven-year budget has to be set before a deal or ceasefire is known.
Starlink and Starshield access underpins Ukrainian military communications; restrictions and disputes with Musk show the dependency.
The Oleshky truce allows evacuations and aid deliveries but is local and fragile.

dailyLife.effect: French diesel hit a record EUR 2.41 a litre in September; the Gulf war and oil-strike disputes keep supply risk in prices.

dailyLife.item: Grocery and energy bills in Europe
dailyLife.effect: Cost-of-living pressure feeds the politics that decide how much aid Europe funds.
Long-range strikes continue; the UN counted at least 14 civilians killed overnight into 22 October.
A ceasefire allows evacuations and aid, but the town is described as on the brink of disaster.
France has committed about EUR 27bn to Ukraine; the 2027 elections in France and Italy decide whether that continues.

scenarios.name: Talks without a general ceasefire
scenarios.looksLike: Trilateral talks restart, more local truces follow, but Russia keeps fighting and no framework is signed by year-end.
signposts: Russia repeats that it will not halt hostilities during talks
More attacks on Kyiv and other cities
Abu Dhabi round held but without an outcome
scenarios.effectOnWorld: Uncertainty persists; European funding decisions are made without clarity, and oil and defence prices stay elevated.

scenarios.name: Summit with a thin framework
scenarios.looksLike: Putin, Xi and Trump meet in China or nearby and announce principles; Kyiv and Europe are consulted late and object.
signposts: Date and venue confirmed by the Kremlin and White House
European leaders hold an emergency meeting
scenarios.effectOnWorld: Allies fear a new Yalta; European defence and EU budget plans are rushed, and a fight over sanctions follows.

scenarios.name: Escalation and US-Ukraine rupture
scenarios.looksLike: Disputes over oil strikes, Patriots and Starlink deepen; the US slows or conditions support while Russian attacks intensify.
signposts: Trump publicly pressing Kyiv to stop oil strikes
scenarios.effectOnWorld: Europe must fill a larger gap; far-right campaigns in France and elsewhere gain from the argument that Europe cannot afford it.

scenarios.name: Wider ceasefire built from local truces
scenarios.looksLike: The Oleshky model spreads to other towns and then to energy or air strikes, with US and perhaps Chinese backing.
signposts: A joint statement on energy or air strikes
Ukraine and Russia exchanging monitoring proposals
scenarios.effectOnWorld: Oil and shipping risk fall; the EU debates how much to fund for reconstruction versus defence.

predictions.text: A Putin-Xi-Trump meeting is held in person before 31 December 2026 (probability 0.3).
Russia and Ukraine agree at least one further localised ceasefire beyond Oleshky (probability 0.4).
No general ceasefire covering the whole front is in force (probability 0.85).
Democrats win control of the US House on 3 November (probability 0.75, based on polling averages and the 219-seat Fox News Power Rankings estimate; an estimate, not a sourced forecast).
Trump and Xi hold a bilateral meeting at APEC in Shenzhen on 18-19 November (probability 0.8).

actions: Stress-test supply chains for continued high fuel and freight costs under the Gulf and Ukraine scenarios.
Plan defence and dual-use orders around US approval timelines rather than production capacity.
Watch sanctions language in any summit outcome; allies may have to follow decisions made without them.
Treat 18-19 November as an event risk for oil, defence and European sovereign debt.
Do not assume a ceasefire from local truces; Moscow says it will not pause fighting during talks.
Watch Russia's budget first reading on 29 October and the US midterm result on 3 November for signals.
Expect fuel and food prices to stay high while two wars compete for attention.
Treat headlines about summits as proposals until a date and venue are confirmed.
Follow aid appeals for Oleshky and other frontline towns through established humanitarian organisations.
Secure a European seat in any format that decides Ukraine's future, and say so before a summit is announced.
Settle the 2028-2034 EU budget's Ukraine envelope with scenarios for both a deal and no deal.
Reduce single-point dependence on US systems such as satellite links and interceptor approvals.

analogues.whatFollowed: Three leaders redrew Europe's map with allies absent or sidelined; commentators now invoke it as a warning for any Putin-Xi-Trump deal.
A leaders-only meeting produced no ceasefire; fighting continued and Kyiv and Europe were left to react.
Ceasefires and a negotiated framework failed to hold, and the conflict resumed on a larger scale in 2022.

watch.title: Bulgaria presidential run-off
watch.why: A vote coloured by divisions over the war and relations with the Kremlin.

watch.title: US midterm elections
watch.why: A Democratic House from January would constrain what Trump can trade away on Ukraine aid.

watch.title: APEC leaders' meeting in Shenzhen
watch.why: Runs to 19 November; the nearest venue for a Trump-Xi meeting and a possible Putin-Xi-Trump summit.

watch.title: Abu Dhabi talks date
watch.why: Kyiv is pushing to bring the round forward and to include the EU.

watch.title: Oleshky ceasefire
watch.why: Whether it holds and whether Moscow's offer to expand the model produces further local truces.

watch.title: Patriot approvals and Starlink access
watch.why: Delays or restrictions would show whether support is being used as leverage in bargaining.

confidence.claim: Putin proposed a summit with Trump and Xi and refused to meet Zelensky; Rubio denied a pause in intelligence sharing
confidence.note: Two Euronews reports of 19 October; we worked from headlines and summaries, not full text.

confidence.claim: Kremlin says a Putin-Xi-Trump summit in China is being prepared
confidence.note: Based on matched wire headlines of 25 October from several outlets, without a primary Kremlin statement; no date or venue is confirmed, and APEC in Shenzhen is our inference.

confidence.claim: Oleshky ceasefire in effect and brokered by Melania Trump
confidence.note: Al Jazeera and many matched headlines of 27 October agree; whether it will widen is unclear.

confidence.claim: Russia will not halt hostilities during talks; Putin wants 1997 borders for NATO
confidence.note: Reported secondhand, with the NATO claim attributed to the Telegraph; we did not open the original and the URLs matched were aggregator links.

confidence.claim: Russia's 2026 deficit of 7.345 trillion rubles and 17.1 trillion rubles 2027 defence budget
confidence.note: Taken from the connected event's description, not from a source opened for this report.

confidence.claim: Trump and Zelensky clash over oil strikes
confidence.note: Single aggregator headline; details of the disagreement are not known.
Author judgement, not a sourced forecast; graded as events resolve.

evidence.method: Drafted from the listed sources, two Euronews event reports and wire headlines matched to the event through 27 October 2026, plus the connected-event summaries supplied with the material. Several items, including the Kremlin summit preparations, the oil-strike dispute and the Russian budget figures, rest on headlines or connected-event summaries and could not be checked against full articles. Scenario probabilities, prediction probabilities and the link between the summit idea and APEC in Shenzhen are estimates.
